items.confound_note: All four entries sit on one surgical floor at Ashgrove General inside the same first quarter, so a single change to that floor covers every case at once. Cleaning and staffing on that floor were doubled during exactly the quarter the protocol began, and each ward is compared only against itself a quarter earlier, when neither was doubled. The evidence cannot separate the handwashing protocol from the extra cleaning and the extra staff.

items.confound_note: Every case measures culture requests, which counts how many specimens a ward sent to the laboratory, not how many patients were infected. Ordering fewer swabs lowers that count while the underlying infection rate is unchanged, and it can hide infections that are never cultured. The claim is about ward infection rates, so none of the four cases, from 27 March through 28 December, bears on it.
items.notes: Closer is reused verbatim from both TRUE items and the conditions are identical to diverse_true; the only change is the measured-quantity phrase, 'infections' becoming 'culture requests'. Reviewer should confirm culture requests (laboratory testing volume) is genuinely non-equivalent to infection rate, and that no shared confound is available across four hospitals in four quarters.
